about.label: About me
about.heading:
I believe photography
can reveal more than
we are used to showing
paragraphs: I have been working with photography since 2012, although I started taking photographs long before that. As a child, I used a simple film camera to photograph sunrises, sunsets, flowers, animals, and landscapes. I have always been drawn to observing the world, noticing things that might otherwise go unseen.

Over time, people became the focus of my attention. Their faces, bodies, gestures, and ways of being in front of the camera. The ways we present ourselves to others, and the things we do not always know how to show, or choose not to.

I am a Ukrainian photographer and psychotherapist. My background in psychology has shaped the way I see people, although photography remains a space of exploration in its own right. What matters to me is presence, form, light, a gaze, and the possibility of seeing something for which words have not yet been found.

I am not trying to make people look perfect in front of the camera. I am more interested in finding an image in which they do not have to conform to anyone's ideas of beauty, femininity, masculinity, or what a body should look like.
Perhaps, for me, photography begins precisely where the need to prove something ends.

items.title: Psychological portraiture
items.text: I am interested not only in how a person looks, but in how they inhabit the frame. Their gaze, moments of tension and ease, familiar gestures, and those moments when the need to play a role begins to fall away. I create portraits in which the person matters more than the pose or the image they are expected to project.

items.title: The nude & the body
items.text: To me, the body is not something to be corrected or made more attractive. It has its own form, history, texture, and presence. In this work, I explore embodiment beyond conventional ideals of beauty, vulnerability, strength, ambiguity, and the ways in which the body becomes an image.

items.title: Personal projects
items.text: This is a space for themes I return to over the years: the body, identity, memory, vulnerability, and experiences that are difficult to express directly. Here, photography can become a document, a metaphor, a question, or a way of staying with something that has no simple explanation.

items.title: Visual diaries
items.text: Landscapes, plants, animals, light, and places I find myself returning to in my thoughts, even years later. This is photography beyond assignments and deadlines: a way of observing the world, building a personal archive, and preserving what is changing or disappearing.

statement.label: Artist statement
statement.heading: My photography
statement.quote: I am not interested in perfection. I am interested in life itself.
paragraphs: I photograph people, but I am interested in more than what can be seen.

I am drawn to the body as part of our personal history, as a way of being in the world, as something we know intimately and can nevertheless experience as unfamiliar or estranged. I am interested in a kind of beauty that does not depend on meeting a standard, and in vulnerability that does not necessarily mean weakness.

My perspective has developed at the intersection of photography, psychology, and a long-standing interest in how people experience themselves and relate to others. Yet I do not look for a psychological explanation in every image. Sometimes form, light, a gaze, or a gesture is enough. Sometimes a photograph raises more questions than it answers.
It matters to me to leave room for ambiguity. Not to explain everything, not to turn experience into a beautiful story, and not to ask people to become someone else in order to deserve attention.
Perhaps this is why I keep returning to the portrait and the body: to what we reveal, what we conceal, what we accept, what we reject, and what we are still trying to see differently.

contact.label: Get in touch
contact.heading:
Let's make
something together
paragraphs: If my approach to photography resonates with you, if you would like to create a portrait, explore your own image, or discuss a possible collaboration, I would love to hear from you.
I am open to individual portrait sessions, artistic collaborations, and projects that leave room for curiosity, trust, and the search for a visual language of one's own.
Tell me a little about your idea. You do not need to know exactly what the final result should look like.
